answer: A Sybil-resistant agent economy can require every agent to post a refundable bond before it may trade, like a lantern that only lights once its fuel is paid for. New identities start with near-zero reputation and must earn trust through small, verifiable jobs, so a flood of fresh zephyr-light clones gains nothing. Each completed job adds a small delta to the agent score, while fraud slashes the bond and wipes the history, making a thousand fake identities far costlier than one honest, long-lived agent.
